items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-07-23, 08-03
items.q: I met Mr. Peterson when I was about, um, I guess 16 years old. He had the little music shop there on Broad by Orleans. Mm-hmm. And, uh, a bunch of us kids would go over there all the time and talk to him.

ctx.x: Pete Fountain talks about that. I think he talks about Harold Peterson's store and how he'd be back in that neighborhood. And, uh, I just wanted, did you know him when you were quite young?

I met Mr. Peterson when I was about, um, I guess 16 years old. He had the little music shop there on Broad by Orleans. Mm-hmm. And, uh, a bunch of us kids would go over there all the time and talk to him. He was, he was, was, I'm speaking about him in the past tense. He was a wonderful man. And, uh, for some reason or another, he took a special interest in the kids. And it wasn't that we spent a whole lot of money in his shop. Mm-hmm. We just, uh, he just liked to see the kids play and was, uh, very helpful in…
Yeah, he always struck me as that kind of man. Everybody's always said that. Who did you see in a shop when you were going there?
